name: Kaya Guides (charityevals' estimate)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: young adults across India, mostly in Hindi-speaking states, reached on WhatsApp.
summary: Kaya Guides runs WHO's guided self-help course for depression, Step-by-Step, on WhatsApp in Hindi for young adults in India: eight weeks of video lessons with short weekly calls from lay guides. In 2025 about 2,800 people started it, at about {{row:cost_per_person}} each. The effect is the three randomised trials of guided Step-by-Step pooled (about half a standard deviation on depression), fading over about a year and a half, cut for trust in the trials and how far they carry to young Indians on WhatsApp and for engagement, plus the suicides it averts. It comes to about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000 (plausible range {{range}}). The biggest uncertainties are how long the effect lasts and how much of the trials' effect carries over; Kaya Guides' own randomised trial, running in 2026, will test both.

source.title: Kaya Guides, cost per participant by month (the data behind its website's cost chart, series 'Kaya Guides (actual)') and its count of new participants per day
source.page: Monthly points for January to December 2025 (the chart's 11th to 22nd points; its last, 1,200 participants at $31.91, is August 2026, which the home page gives as ~$32), times new participants per month from https://kayaguides.com/_file/data/participants-per-day.e7029d7a.parquet

rows.explainer: Kaya Guides publishes no accounts of its own: it is a project of Development Consortium in India and fiscally sponsored by Players Philanthropy Fund in the US, and neither reports its costs separately. Its website's cost chart gives the total cost per participant each month (all costs, partnerships and overhead included, footnote 43), and its participant file gives new participants per day. The chart's months line up with the participant counts (its points are each month's new participants rounded: 94, 135, 64 ... 482 in 2025 against 90, 100, 60 ... 500), so each month's cost per participant × that month's new participants, summed over January to December 2025, is the year's spending: about $10,500 a month in the first half rising to $20,000 by December, $166,981 in all. Range $150,000 (the chart's rounded counts give $156,000) to $190,000 (months whose denominator differs from new participants). For comparison, Kaya Guides gave its 2024 budget as $160,000 (its funding post of 26 November 2023, forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/CdELxtHgQjzCYPhtm) and projected $313,504 for 2025 (its pilot-results post of 16 June 2024, forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/6NaRJpSn2zfRSnGYN); the derived figure is lower because the programme grew more slowly than planned.

rows.label: Precision weight of the Syrian trial
rows.explainer: Inverse-variance weights, as in a fixed-effect meta-analysis.

rows.label: Precision weight of the Lebanese trial
rows.explainer: As above.

rows.label: Effect on depression at the end of the course (SD), the three guided Step-by-Step trials pooled
rows.explainer: The precision-weighted mean of every randomised trial of guided Step-by-Step with a published effect on depression: the programme Kaya Guides delivers, with the same eight weekly lessons and short weekly contacts by a nonspecialist. Left out: the self-guided Egyptian trial (small effects; no guide), the Swiss-German trial (over 90% dropout, no conclusion) and the 138-person Lebanese feasibility trial (Heim et al. 2021: complete cases only, over 60% dropout). Kaya Guides has no controlled evaluation yet (an RCT is running in 2026); its own pre-post data, a fall of 5.9 PHQ-9 points among the 23% who answered the 8-week survey, has no control group and is a check, not a trial: the Lebanese trials' control arms improved by several points too. A larger review of digital psychological interventions in low- and middle-income countries (Fu et al. 2020, Lancet Psychiatry, 22 trials: g = 0.60, 0.45 to 0.75) is a cross-check.

rows.label: Years until the effect has faded

source.title: Cuijpers P et al. (2022), Effects of a WHO-guided digital health intervention for depression in Syrian refugees in Lebanon: a randomized controlled trial, PLOS Medicine 19(6):e1004025
source.page: Abstract, Methods and findings (3-month follow-up); with Li et al. 2024 (China), Results
source.quote: Significant effects on all outcomes were maintained at 3 months follow-up.

rows.explainer: 1.5 years (6 months to 3 years) for a straight fade to zero, from the trials' follow-ups, all 3 months after the course: the Syrian trial 0.61 SD (0.37 to 0.85), the Lebanese 0.52 (0.22 to 0.82), the Chinese 0.16 (-0.07 to 0.40). Pooled by precision like the end-of-treatment effects (standard errors 0.122, 0.153 and 0.120), they come to 0.41 SD, 83% of the pooled 0.50 at the end of treatment; a straight line that keeps 83% at a quarter of a year reaches zero at about 1.45 years. The individual-patient meta-analysis of internet CBT (Karyotaki et al. 2021, JAMA Psychiatry) found guided self-help still ahead of controls at 6 to 12 months, which a shorter fade would contradict. The low end is the Chinese trial alone (zero at about half a year); the high end allows for the Syrian trial's effect, still rising at 3 months.

rows.label: Discount factor for the fading effect
rows.formula: if(continuous_discount_rate > 0, (continuous_discount_rate * effect_duration_years - 1 + exp(-(continuous_discount_rate * effect_duration_years))) / (0.5 * (continuous_discount_rate * effect_duration_years) * (continuous_discount_rate * effect_duration_years)), 1)
rows.explainer: Present value of the triangle (linear fade to zero) at the shared rate, as a share of its undiscounted area; as in the HLI models.

rows.label: Total effect per person (SD-years, discounted)
rows.explainer: Area of the triangle: linear decay from the initial effect to zero, discounted.

rows.label: WELLBYs per person treated
rows.explainer: SD-years into WELLBYs at the site's one rate (@wellby_factors). The WELLBY slider then puts WELLBYs into healthy years, calibrated so a year of depression is worth the same here as through the GBD weights (@depression); never convert depression into DALYs inside this model.

rows.label: Household size
rows.explainer: The site's figure for India (facts/household_size.json). Participants are mostly 18 to 29 and many live with their parents or in-laws, so the household is about the national average.

rows.label: Household multiplier (recipient plus spillovers)
rows.explainer: Each other household member gains the site's one share of the recipient's effect (HLI's, @wellby_factors).

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.64 (0.4 to 0.9), two parts. Internal, 0.85: the trials are run by the programme's developers, outcomes are self-reported and participants knew their arm, and over half of the intervention arm missed the end-of-treatment assessment (the Syrian trial 152 of 283; 167 by the 3-month follow-up), with missing outcomes imputed. The trials' own attrition bounds anchor the cut: in the Syrian trial the worst-case (Lee) bounds point the same way but are no longer significant, in the Lebanese trial the effect stays significant under them. No publication-bias cut: the pool is every randomised trial of guided Step-by-Step, and the programme's weak and null trials are published too. External, 0.75: the one trial in young adults (China) found 0.70 of the pooled effect, the closest anchor for Kaya Guides' young Hindi-speaking participants recruited through Instagram, lifted a little because that trial's support was the lightest and the pooled trials themselves vary; the course is on WhatsApp rather than the trials' app, with 15-minute guide calls. After this and the adjustments below, the effect counted is about {{row:total_adj}} of the pooled trials' effect.

rows.label: Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: 1 (0.9 to 1): the trials' effect is against enhanced care as usual (psychoeducation and referral), which already includes what controls found for themselves. These participants have even less: 85% of Indians with depression get no treatment (Kaya Guides' home page, citing the National Mental Health Survey 2015-16), and a therapy session costs about two-fifths of a casual worker's weekly pay. The low end allows for a few who would have paid for therapy.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: Judgment 95% (85 to 100%): Kaya Guides pays its guides, technology and ads itself, and its cost figure includes its partnerships (footnote 43). WHO wrote the course (an adaptation of its openly licensed Step-by-Step, a past contribution not used up here) and Development Consortium hosts the project in India; their staff time is the small remainder.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Delivery adjustment (fidelity, compliance, follow-through)
rows.explainer: Judgment 95% (80 to 100%). The trials' effects are intention to treat, so their own non-starters and dropouts are already in them (in the Syrian trial 72% finished the introduction session and 32% all sessions; in the Lebanese 60% and 19%). Kaya Guides' participants complete 3.8 of 8 calls on average and 53% are still active 30 days after joining (its statistics file, last 12 months), engagement in the trials' range. The remaining 5% is for joiners counted in the participant file who never take a first call (the home page's 48-hour figure excludes those who booked and never answered); the low end allows that share to be larger.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: 1, measured: the charity's own count of who started the programme (2,776 in 2025) meets an effect from randomised trials of the same intervention delivered the same way (WHO's guided Step-by-Step, digital lessons with weekly short contacts by a nonspecialist helper). How far those trials carry to young Indians on WhatsApp is in evidence_adj. Kaya Guides' own randomised trial, running in 2026, should replace the pooled trials when it reports.

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Effects not modelled above, as a share of the modelled value
rows.explainer: +2% (-3 to +8%): the trials found matching falls in anxiety and post-traumatic stress and gains in functioning, mostly the same change the depression scale already counts; participants' accounts of leaving abusive homes or returning to work or college add a little. A risk on the other side: a self-help course for people in severe episodes (mean PHQ-9 17.8, many with suicidal thoughts) could delay more intensive care for a few; Kaya Guides screens and refers, and no harm was found in the trials.
